draft.draft_body: {"type":"doc","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"When I say I want to build a legacy, I can make the sentence sound nobler than a wish for fame. That comfort disappears when I ask a harder question: would the work still function if I stopped?"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I have been using that question to separate three things we often confuse: virality, fame, and legacy. The framework helped me see the difference, but it also carried a flattering assumption. I had treated legacy as the natural reward for building something good enough."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"That is where the framework needed another pass. Durable work depends on more than quality. It needs adoption, reinterpretation, and people willing to hold it when its maker no longer can."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The test that survives"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Virality, fame, and legacy differ most clearly in how quickly they decay, where their value sits, and how much they depend on the creator. A viral post may lose its force within 24 hours. Fame can last for years, sometimes for a generation, but it remains tied to a name. Legacy can last for decades because its value has moved into something other people use."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Three parts of this framework still seem right to me. The most useful is the decoupling test, by which I mean asking whether the work still functions when I stop. If the work requires my voice, presence, or constant repair, then its life remains attached to mine."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Half-life gives the question a timescale. Popularity tells us little about survival through a funding cycle, a change of leadership, or neglect. Virality, fame, and legacy also describe different outcomes rather than stages of one journey. Enough attention does not mature into permanence. A famous person can leave no durable structure, while an almost forgotten person can shape a practice used every day."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Still, the framework made attention look like the enemy. That was too simple."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Attention has a job"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Attention helps adoption. A standard, tool, or idea becomes part of ordinary life only after people notice it, test it, argue about it, and decide to carry it forward. Good design cannot place itself into the world."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The history of networking contains two separate stories that are easy to collapse. On January 1, 1983, ARPANET began its planned cutover from NCP to TCP/IP. "},{"type":"text","text":"RFC 801","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc801.txt"}}]},{"type":"text","text":", published in 1981, laid out the transition with relay hosts speaking both protocols, so NCP did not vanish everywhere at once."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"A different contest unfolded later. OSI, the international committee effort to define how networks should talk, published its Basic Reference Model as ISO 7498 in 1984. The model was architecturally sound, and many expected the OSI protocol suite to prevail through the late 1980s and early 1990s, encouraged by government mandates such as GOSIP. Yet the suite was costly, slow to arrive, and often not implemented. TCP/IP spread through running code, free BSD implementations, and the IETF's rough consensus, while ISO documents carried costs and delays. Andrew L. Russell tells that history in "},{"type":"text","text":"“OSI: The Internet That Wasn't”","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"https://spectrum.ieee.org/osi-the-internet-that-wasnt"}}]},{"type":"text","text":"."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Technical merit mattered, but adoption had its own force. People had to distribute the protocols, implement them, teach them, and trust that other people would do the same. Working systems gave those choices momentum."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Reputation can help a useful artifact cross the gap between existence and use. A trusted name may persuade a stranger to read a specification or try a tool. Attention becomes corrosive when accumulating an audience becomes the purpose of the work."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Refusing all attention can become another form of vanity, especially when the work needs people before it can matter. I try to remember what the attention is for."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Permanence is the wrong promise"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I once described legacy as a permanent modification to baseline reality. I no longer think permanence is a serious target. It is a romantic word that hides how human structures actually survive."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Institutions get captured. Standards are superseded. Philosophies are read selectively under conditions their authors could not imagine. Even an old idea changes as each generation decides what to keep, discard, or bend toward a new purpose."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The better target is durability across reinterpretation. A legacy survives because it can be revised without becoming useless. It persists through argument, translation, partial loss, and changes in ownership."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Authorial intent has no special protection here. People may misunderstand the work, improve it, or preserve the part its author considered least important. Insisting on control would preserve my name while denying the work useful independence."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The thought is uncomfortable because authorship feels like a moral claim. I made this, so I should decide what it means. Durable work asks me to let my interpretation become one voice rather than the final court of appeal."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"The missing column is custody"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"This leads to the largest correction. Engineering can make an artifact correct. Governance gives it a chance to survive."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"The original framework compared decay, value, and dependence on the creator. It was missing a column: "},{"type":"text","text":"custody","marks":[{"type":"bold"}]},{"type":"text","text":". Who holds the thing when the author is gone?"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Custody means more than storage. A public repository can remain online while its purpose quietly dies. Someone must interpret the work, accept changes, reject bad ones, settle disputes, transfer authority, and teach new people why it exists."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Without a custodian, a project becomes an abandoned repo, a standard nobody implements, or a fork guided by a different purpose. None of these outcomes is automatically tragic. They simply show that persistence of files and persistence of function are different achievements."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Python offers a concrete case. Guido van Rossum stepped down as BDFL in July 2018. "},{"type":"text","text":"PEP 13","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"https://peps.python.org/pep-0013/"}}]},{"type":"text","text":" established an elected steering council, the first council was seated in 2019, and releases continued under that governance."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Governance also has to survive its current governors. A project held together by one benevolent maintainer has only deferred the problem. Real custody includes succession: a way for judgment and authority to move before absence turns into crisis. That leaves me with a stricter sentence:"}]},{"type":"blockquote","content":[{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Legacy is what other people can carry without you."}]}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Carrying implies effort and freedom. The next custodian must be able to repair the work and also change it. If every meaningful decision still requires the founder's blessing, custody has never really moved."}]},{"type":"heading","attrs":{"level":2},"content":[{"type":"text","text":"Applying the test to my own work"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I am building "},{"type":"text","text":"MCP Visor","marks":[{"type":"link","attrs":{"href":"https://github.com/themayursinha/mcp-visor"}}]},{"type":"text","text":", a public, MIT-licensed, self-hosted proxy. It intercepts MCP "},{"type":"text","text":"tools/call","marks":[{"type":"code"}]},{"type":"text","text":" requests before relay and evaluates them against policy. The repository describes its purpose as runtime policy enforcement for MCP tool execution."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Applying the custody test turns my attention away from another release and toward two unanswered questions. Does anyone run this who has never spoken to me? Is there someone else with the judgment and the commit rights to say no?"}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"Those questions are harder than writing more code because effort still leaves me at the center. A durable project would need enough context for someone else to make decisions, including decisions I might have made differently. Authority would have to move as well."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"That prospect exposes the emotional part of custody. I like being able to say that I built the thing. Shared authority weakens the clean line between the work and my identity, even as it gives the work a better chance of continuing."}]},{"type":"paragraph","content":[{"type":"text","text":"I do not yet know the answer to either question. For now, they tell me what remains unfinished."}]}]}
draft.draft_subtitle: Would the work still function if you stopped?
